title: Wheel of Fortune under Razorkin Needlehead and Torbran: 21 to each opponent from Needlehead alone

you: Razorkin Needlehead (2/2; untapped, no summoning sickness)
Torbran, Thane of Red Fell (2/4; untapped)

scenario.mana_available: {W}{U} or any two (Command Tower and Hallowed Fountain, untapped)

stack.object: Wheel of Fortune — 'Each player discards their hand, then draws seven cards.'
stack.note: cast from your hand in your precombat main phase, paid {2}{R} with Mountain, Sacred Foundry and Steam Vents; it was the last card in your hand

extras.note_for_the_resolver: Your turn, precombat main phase. Nobody responds to anything. Both your commanders are in the command zone and play no part. Every library is far larger than seven, so nobody draws from an empty library. You take no other actions.
assumptions: No player has a replacement effect on drawing or damage other than Torbran.
No opponent controls a creature or a damage-prevention effect.

scenario.question: After Wheel of Fortune and every trigger it causes have resolved: how many times does Razorkin Needlehead's ability trigger for each opponent, how much damage does each trigger deal with Torbran, Thane of Red Fell on the battlefield, and what is each opponent's life total?

steps.action: All players pass priority; Wheel of Fortune (the only object on the stack) resolves.
steps.effect: Nobody responds, so the top (only) object on the stack, Wheel of Fortune, begins to resolve.

citations.quote: When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.

steps.action: Wheel of Fortune: each player discards their hand, then draws seven cards, in the order written.
steps.effect: Instructions are followed in order: first every player discards their hand (yours is already empty — Wheel was your last card; the opponents discard 4, 3 and 2 cards), then every player draws seven. You, the active player, draw your seven first, then each opponent draws seven in turn order. Your own draws trigger nothing: Needlehead triggers only on an OPPONENT drawing.

citations.quote: The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written.
If more than one player is instructed to draw cards, the active player performs all of their draws first, then each other player in turn order does the same.

steps.action: Each opponent's 'draw seven' is seven individual draws; Razorkin Needlehead triggers once per card drawn.
steps.effect: Drawing seven is seven separate card draws, each one an occurrence of Needlehead's trigger event ('Whenever an opponent draws a card'). Needlehead therefore triggers 7 times for each opponent — 21 triggers in total, each one tied to the opponent whose draw caused it (the ability deals damage 'to them'). The Needlehead ruling (only cards actually 'drawn' count) agrees: Wheel says 'draws'. The triggers do nothing yet; they wait while Wheel finishes resolving, and Wheel goes to your graveyard.

citations.quote: If a player is instructed to draw multiple cards, that player performs that many individual card draws.
An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.
The ability doesn’t do anything at this point.
As the final part of an instant or sorcery spell’s resolution, the spell is put into its owner’s graveyard.

steps.action: Wheel of Fortune has finished resolving; before anyone receives priority the game checks state-based actions, and only then are the waiting triggers put on the stack.
steps.effect: The active player would now receive priority, so the game first checks state-based actions. Nobody has lost life yet (every player is still at 40), nobody drew from an empty library (every library holds well over seven), and no creature has lethal damage or 0 toughness (Razorkin Needlehead is 2/2 and Torbran 2/4, both undamaged), so no state-based action is performed. With nothing performed, the 21 waiting Needlehead triggers are put on the stack next (step 5), after which the check is repeated and again finds nothing.

citations.quote: Whenever a player would get priority (see rule 117, “Timing and Priority”), the game checks for any of the listed conditions for state-based actions, then performs all applicable state-based actions simultaneously as a single event.

If any state-based actions are performed as a result of a check, the check is repeated; otherwise all triggered abilities that are waiting to be put on the stack are put on the stack, then the check is repeated.

Each time a player would get priority, the game first performs all applicable state-based actions as a single event (see rule 704, “State-Based Actions”), then repeats this process until no state-based actions are performed. Then triggered abilities are put on the stack (see rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities”).
The active player receives priority after a spell or ability (other than a mana ability) resolves.

steps.action: After the state-based-action check finds nothing to do, you put all 21 Needlehead triggers on the stack in an order of your choice.
steps.effect: You control all 21 triggers, so you stack them in any order; the order changes nothing, since every trigger is independent and no opponent can reach 0 before all have resolved (see step 7). The active player then receives priority.

citations.quote: Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.
each player, in APNAP order, puts each triggered ability they control with a trigger condition that isn’t another ability triggering on the stack in any order they choose.
The active player receives priority after a spell or ability (other than a mana ability) resolves.

steps.action: Each Needlehead trigger resolves (all players pass each time): Needlehead deals 1 damage to that opponent, which Torbran replaces with 3.
steps.effect: Razorkin Needlehead is a red source you control (colors: R) dealing damage to an opponent, so Torbran's replacement effect ('it deals that much damage plus 2 instead') applies to each damage event separately as it happens: each trigger deals 1 + 2 = 3 damage. The extra 2 is dealt by Needlehead itself (per Torbran's official ruling). No other replacement or prevention effect exists (scenario assumption). Damage to a player from a source without infect is life loss, so each trigger costs its opponent 3 life.

citations.quote: replacement effects apply continuously as events happen—they aren’t locked in ahead of time.
Effects that use the word “instead” are replacement effects.
Second, damage is dealt, as modified by replacement and prevention effects that interact with damage.
Damage dealt to a player by a source without infect causes that player to lose that much life.
When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.

steps.action: State-based actions are checked each time a player would receive priority — after every one of the 21 triggers resolves — and no player is ever at 0 or less life.
steps.effect: After each trigger resolves the active player would receive priority, so the game checks state-based actions before that happens. The worst a seat can be at mid-sequence is 40 - 3 x 7 = 19, so no check ever finds a player at 0 or less life, and no creature is affected (Needlehead, a 2/2, and Torbran, a 2/4, take no damage). Each opponent takes 7 x 3 = 21 damage across their seven triggers: 40 - 21 = 19. No player loses the game. After the last trigger resolves the final check also finds nothing, the stack is empty, and the game continues in your precombat main phase.

citations.quote: Whenever a player would get priority (see rule 117, “Timing and Priority”), the game checks for any of the listed conditions for state-based actions, then performs all applicable state-based actions simultaneously as a single event.

Each time a player would get priority, the game first performs all applicable state-based actions as a single event (see rule 704, “State-Based Actions”), then repeats this process until no state-based actions are performed. Then triggered abilities are put on the stack (see rule 603, “Handling Triggered Abilities”).
The active player receives priority after a spell or ability (other than a mana ability) resolves.
If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.

final_state.summary: Needlehead triggers 7 times for each opponent (21 triggers total); with Torbran each trigger deals 3 damage (1 + 2), so each opponent takes 21 and goes from 40 to 19. That is 21 per seat, 63 across the pod — not lethal to anyone. You drew seven (no triggers), and your hand is the seven new cards; Wheel of Fortune is in your graveyard.

findings.note: Wheel of Fortune is the only object on the stack, so when every player passes it resolves.

Wheel says 'discards their hand, then draws seven' (cards.json oracle), so every discard comes before any draw. The rest of 608.2c (replacement effects can modify the actions) does not apply: the scenario names no draw replacement.
The active player draws first, then each opponent in turn order. Needlehead's oracle is 'Whenever an opponent draws a card', so the controller's own seven draws trigger nothing.
Full text: 'Cards may only be drawn one at a time.' Seven cards means seven separate draws.

Read with 121.2: one trigger per draw, 7 per opponent, 21 in total. Agrees with the Needlehead ruling (2024-09-20): 'If a spell or ability causes an opponent to put cards into their hand without specifically using the word "draw," it's not a card drawn.' Wheel does use 'draws'.
Triggers do nothing until they are put on the stack.
Wheel goes to its owner's graveyard as the last part of its resolution.

Fixes round-1 finding 704.3. Both quotes are verbatim from 704.3. The full rule sets the order: check SBAs, then put waiting triggers on the stack, then check again, then a player gets priority. Step 4 states that order exactly. The SBA check after Wheel resolves is now an explicit step.
Same order: SBAs first, then triggered abilities, then the player who would have received priority does so.
The active player is the one who would receive priority after Wheel resolves, and that is what starts the check.
Triggers go on the stack the next time a player would receive priority.

The quote is a verbatim fragment. You control all 21 triggers (none is a trigger on another ability triggering), so you choose their order. The rest of 603.3b (SBAs re-checked afterwards) matches step 4's 'the check is repeated'. Order does not matter: each trigger resolves the same way and no seat can reach 0.
Read with 117.5: the active player gets priority once the triggers are on the stack.
Torbran applies separately to each damage event as it happens.

Torbran's oracle 'it deals that much damage plus 2 instead' makes it a replacement effect. Needlehead's colors are [R] in cards.json, so it is 'a red source you control', and 1 becomes 3. Agrees with Torbran's ruling (2019-10-04): 'The additional 2 damage is dealt by the same source as the original source of damage.' Torbran's ordering ruling (2019-10-04) does not apply, because the scenario assumes no other damage-modifying effect.
Damage is dealt as modified by replacement effects.
Needlehead has no infect (oracle checked), so 3 damage is 3 life lost.
Each trigger resolves after all players pass in succession.
SBAs are checked every time a player would get priority, which is after each of the 21 resolutions.
Same timing as 704.3, stated from the priority side.
The active player receives priority after each trigger resolves, so a check happens before each one.

The loss condition is never met. Arithmetic: 7 x 3 = 21 per seat, 40 - 21 = 19. The 63 pod total is stated separately and labelled as the pod total, matching scenario-facts drain_arithmetic (3 opponents at 40). Final libraries 52-7=45, 61-7=54 and 47-7=40, and hands of 7, all check out.
Fixes round-1 finding 208.1. scenario.board now lists Razorkin Needlehead as 2/2, matching cards.json (power 2, toughness 2). Torbran 2/4 also matches. Steps 4 and 7 use 2/2 consistently.

The only replacement effect is Torbran (614), applied per event. No triggers fire beyond Needlehead's: the opponents' discards and your own draws trigger nothing on this board. No combat.
